# Abstract

This gazetteer traces the population histories of 245 cities, frontline towns, regional capitals, military garrisons and industrial centres across Ukraine, Belarus and the Russian Federation between 2021 and 2026 (Figure \ref{fig:hero} and Table \ref{tab:gaz-summary}). Organised across the 123 administrative and occupation-history divisions of the war theatre - 33 divisions spanning Ukraine's 27 constitutional oblasts and special-status cities, 7 administrative divisions in Belarus and 83 federal subjects in the Russian Federation - the tables record the urban demographic consequences of full-scale warfare, siege destruction, internal displacement and regional mobilisation.

Across Ukraine, frontline towns in Donetsk, Luhansk, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson Oblasts suffered near-total depopulation under artillery and aerial bombardment, while Kyiv, Dnipro, Lviv and western regional centres expanded or stabilised as reception hubs for millions of internally displaced citizens. In Belarus and the Russian Federation, urban populations reflected the contrast between demographic stability in Moscow, Saint Petersburg, hydrocarbon boomtowns and major defence-industrial hubs, evacuation losses in shelled border towns such as Shebekino and Sudzha and steady contraction across peripheral garrison and mono-industrial towns.

# Methodology

With Ukraine's planned 2023 census suspended under martial law and granular municipal series curtailed in Russian statistical releases after 2022, urban population estimates for 2021 to 2026 are reconstructed from municipal administrative registers, displacement surveys and satellite damage assessments [@libanova2024demographic; @iom2025returns; @belstat2024chislennost; @rosstat2024demografiya; @mediazona2025casualties]. Every one of the 123 regional divisions is represented by its administrative seat alongside principal frontline, garrison or industrial towns.

For Ukrainian settlements, pre-invasion 2021 baselines from the State Statistics Service of Ukraine are updated through 2022, 2024 and 2026 using Oblast Military Administration evacuation logs, IOM municipal displacement and returnee series, Copernicus Sentinel-1 radar and UNOSAT optical building-damage surveys and VIIRS night-time light series [@ukrstat2022chiselnist; @acled2025ukraine; @deepstate2025map; @scher2023sar; @unosat2023mariupol]. For Belarusian and Russian cities, municipal baselines from Belstat and the 2021 All-Russian Census are adjusted for wartime emigration, border evacuations in Belgorod and Kursk Oblasts, defence-industrial labour inflows and garrison casualty attrition.

```{r gazetteer-load, include=FALSE}
map_df <- jsonlite::fromJSON((if (file.exists("invasion_settlement_oblast_map.json")) "invasion_settlement_oblast_map.json" else "../../_shared/_gis_cache/invasion_settlement_oblast_map.json"))

clean_tbl_str <- function (x) {
  x <- gsub("([0-9]{4})AD\\b", "\\1", as.character(x), perl = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("([0-9]+,[1-9]+)0+(?![0-9])", "\\1", gsub("([0-9]+),0+(?![0-9])", "\\1", x, perl = TRUE), perl = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Sievierodonetsk", "Sievierodo-netsk", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Syevyerodonetskyi", "Syevyerodo-netskyi", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Kostiantynivka", "Kostianty-nivka", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Dnipropetrovsk", "Dnipro-petrovsk", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Nizhnevartovsk", "Nizhnevar-tovsk", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Severobaykalsk", "Severobay-kalsk", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Blagoveshchensk", "Blagovesh-chensk", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Krasnohorivka", "Krasno-horivka", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Kakhovka", "Kakhov-ka", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Kropyvnytskyi", "Kropyvnyt-skyi", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Khmelnytskyi", "Khmelnyt-skyi", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Zakarpattia", "Zakar-pattia", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Novorossiysk", "Novoros-siysk", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Nefteyugansk", "Nefte-yugansk", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky", "Petropav-lovsk-Kamchatsky", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Yekaterinburg", "Yekaterin-burg", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Magnitogorsk", "Magnito-gorsk", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Novokuznetsk", "Novokuz-netsk", x, fixed = TRUE)
  return(x)
}

fmt_int <- function (v) {
  x <- as.numeric(v)
  if (is.na(x)) return("-")
  if (abs(x) >= 1e6) {
    s <- sprintf("%.2f", x / 1e6)
    s <- sub("\\.?0+$", "", s)
    return(paste0(gsub(".", ",", s, fixed = TRUE), "M"))
  } else if (abs(x) >= 1e3) {
    s <- sprintf("%.1f", x / 1e3)
    if (abs(x) < 1e4 && round(x) %% 100 != 0) {
      s <- sprintf("%.2f", x / 1e3)
    }
    s <- sub("\\.?0+$", "", s)
    return(paste0(gsub(".", ",", s, fixed = TRUE), "k"))
  } else {
    return(as.character(as.integer(round(x))))
  }
}

fmt_pct <- function (p21, p26) {
  ch <- (as.numeric(p26) - as.numeric(p21)) / as.numeric(p21) * 100
  s <- gsub(".", ",", sprintf("%+.1f%%", ch), fixed = TRUE)
  sub(",0%$", "%", s)
}

fmt_coords <- function (lat, lon) {
  s <- gsub("\\.", ",", sprintf("%.2fN, %.2fE", lat, lon))
  s <- gsub("([0-9]+,[1-9]+)0+([NE])", "\\1\\2", s, perl = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("([0-9]+),0+([NE])", "\\1\\2", s, perl = TRUE)
  return(s)
}

build_country_gaz_df <- function (cn) {
  sub_m <- map_df[map_df$country == cn, , drop = FALSE]
  sub_m <- sub_m[order(sub_m$obl_idx, -sub_m$p2021), , drop = FALSE]
  obl_col <- gsub(" Oblast", " Obl.", clean_tbl_str(paste0(sub_m$oblast_name, " (", sub_m$iso, ")")), fixed = TRUE)
  data.frame(
    Settlement = clean_tbl_str(sub_m$name),
    Oblast = obl_col,
    Coords = mapply(fmt_coords, sub_m$lat, sub_m$lon),
    P2021 = vapply(sub_m$p2021, fmt_int, character(1)),
    P2022 = vapply(sub_m$p2022, fmt_int, character(1)),
    P2024 = vapply(sub_m$p2024, fmt_int, character(1)),
    P2026 = vapply(sub_m$p2026, fmt_int, character(1)),
    Change = mapply(fmt_pct, sub_m$p2021, sub_m$p2026),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
```

```{r tab-gaz-summary, echo=FALSE}
sum_rows <- lapply(c("Ukraine", "Belarus", "Russia"), function (cn) {
  sub_m <- map_df[map_df$country == cn, , drop = FALSE]
  data.frame(
    Country = cn,
    Admin1Units = as.character(length(unique(sub_m$iso))),
    Settlements = as.character(nrow(sub_m)),
    Urban2021 = fmt_int(sum(sub_m$p2021)),
    Urban2026 = fmt_int(sum(sub_m$p2026)),
    Change = fmt_pct(sum(sub_m$p2021), sum(sub_m$p2026)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_sum <- rbind(do.call(rbind, sum_rows), data.frame(
  Country = "Total Domain",
  Admin1Units = "123",
  Settlements = as.character(nrow(map_df)),
  Urban2021 = fmt_int(sum(map_df$p2021)),
  Urban2026 = fmt_int(sum(map_df$p2026)),
  Change = fmt_pct(sum(map_df$p2021), sum(map_df$p2026)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
))
render_table_template(
  df_sum,
  list(
    caption = "Regional distribution and combined population of the 245 catalogued urban settlements across Ukraine, Belarus and the Russian Federation.",
    col_names = c("Country", "Divisions", "Settlements", "2021", "2026", "Change"),
    label = "tab:gaz-summary"
  )
)
```

# Results

## Ukrainian Oblasts and Occupation Zones

In Ukraine, urban trajectories between 2021 and 2026 diverged sharply along the line of contact (Table \ref{tab:gaz-ua}). Frontline cities and towns subjected to siege and protracted artillery battles - including Bakhmut, Avdiivka, Popasna, Vuhledar, Marinka, Vovchansk and Kupiansk - lost over 85% to 99% of their pre-war inhabitants, while Mariupol, Sievierodonetsk, Lysychansk and Kherson City contracted to a fraction of their 2021 populations. Conversely, central and western regional capitals such as Kyiv, Dnipro, Poltava, Vinnytsia, Lviv, Ivano-Frankivsk, Chernivtsi and Uzhhorod absorbed large inflows of internally displaced residents.

```{r tab-gaz-ua, echo=FALSE}
df_gaz_ua <- build_country_gaz_df("Ukraine")
render_table_template(
  df_gaz_ua,
  list(
    caption = sprintf("Coordinates and resident population trajectories for %d Ukrainian cities and frontline towns across 33 oblast and occupation-history divisions, 2021-2026.", nrow(df_gaz_ua)),
    col_names = c("Settlement", "Oblast / Occupation Zone (ISO)", "Coords", "2021", "2022", "2024", "2026", "Change"),
    label = "tab:gaz-ua"
  )
)
```

## Belarusian Oblasts and Minsk City

Across the six oblasts of Belarus and Minsk City, urban populations experienced gradual contraction or stagnation between 2021 and 2026 (Table \ref{tab:gaz-by}). Natural decrease and skilled emigration to Poland and Lithuania weighed on Minsk, Gomel, Mogilev, Vitebsk and Bobruisk, while southern staging towns in Brest and Gomel Oblasts saw modest outflows following the 2022 northern offensive.

```{r tab-gaz-by, echo=FALSE}
df_gaz_by <- build_country_gaz_df("Belarus")
render_table_template(
  df_gaz_by,
  list(
    caption = sprintf("Coordinates and resident population trajectories for %d Belarusian regional capitals and industrial centres across all 7 administrative divisions, 2021-2026.", nrow(df_gaz_by)),
    col_names = c("Settlement", "Oblast / Capital (ISO)", "Coords", "2021", "2022", "2024", "2026", "Change"),
    label = "tab:gaz-by"
  )
)
```

## Russian Federal Subjects

Across the 83 federal subjects of the Russian Federation, urban population changes between 2021 and 2026 reflected border bombardment, defence-industrial mobilisation and regional demographic differentials (Table \ref{tab:gaz-ru}). Shelled frontier towns in Belgorod and Kursk Oblasts (Shebekino and Sudzha) lost substantial shares of their civilian residents, whereas Kursk City absorbed displaced border villagers, hydrocarbon centres in Khanty-Mansi and Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrugs (Surgut, Nizhnevartovsk and Novy Urengoy) and North Caucasian capitals (Makhachkala, Grozny and Nazran) recorded steady growth and northern garrison and mining towns continued to contract.

```{r tab-gaz-ru, echo=FALSE}
df_gaz_ru <- build_country_gaz_df("Russia")
render_table_template(
  df_gaz_ru,
  list(
    caption = sprintf("Coordinates and resident population trajectories for %d Russian regional capitals, garrison towns and industrial centres across all 83 federal subjects, 2021-2026.", nrow(df_gaz_ru)),
    col_names = c("Settlement", "Federal Subject (ISO)", "Coords", "2021", "2022", "2024", "2026", "Change"),
    label = "tab:gaz-ru"
  )
)
```
